passage:
A video game set in an ancient city became popular at school. Students liked exploring streets, markets, temples, and homes.
Their history teacher saw an opportunity. She asked students to compare the game with real historical sources. They found many accurate details, but also some changes made for fun or easier play.
The class learned that historical games can create interest, but they are not textbooks.
One student said the game made him want to learn what was real.
The teacher accepted that as success. Entertainment can open the door to history, but careful reading must walk through it.
